test_title: SSC CPO 2025 Official Paper (Held On 12 Dec, 2025 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: According to the 1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship, what is one key provision agreed upon by both governments?

options.text: No diplomatic ties between India and Nepal
Reciprocal rights of residence and trade

solution:
The correct answer is __**Reciprocal rights of residence and trade**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/e3594069eb4eac3d559af7c626aabe4ee4145967932cf8ad78e35476f134a4b8.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The **1950 India-Nepal Treaty of Peace and Friendship** was signed on **31 July 1950** in **Kathmandu** by the last Rana Prime Minister of Nepal, **Mohun Shamsher Jang Bahadur Rana**, and the Indian Ambassador to Nepal, **Chandeshwar Prasad Narain Singh**.
 
• **Article 7** of the treaty is a cornerstone provision that mandates both governments to grant, on a reciprocal basis, to the nationals of one country in the territories of the other, the same privileges in matters of **residence**, **ownership of property**, and participation in **trade and commerce**.
 
• This provision effectively created a unique **open border** system, allowing citizens of both nations to move freely across the **1,850 km** boundary without the requirement of a **visa** or **passport** for employment and residency.
 
• The treaty aims to maintain 'everlasting peace and friendship' and requires both nations to inform each other of any serious friction or misunderstanding with any neighboring state likely to cause any breach in the friendly relations subsisting between the two governments.
 
• It reinforces the **sovereignty** and **territorial integrity** of both nations while formalizing a 'special relationship' that transcends standard diplomatic protocols due to shared cultural and historical ties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3e20068b61817b168623bbf4377a66602deb382bfb1e34ae29a5e35078dcefcb.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Strategic and Economic Context**:
 
 
• **Himalayan Security**: The treaty was signed during a period of significant geopolitical change in Asia, intended to secure the **Himalayan frontier** as a natural defense barrier for the Indian subcontinent.
 
• **Transit Rights**: As a **landlocked country**, Nepal benefits from the treaty and subsequent agreements that facilitate the transit of goods through Indian territory to international sea ports like **Kolkata** and **Haldia**.
 
• **Roti-Beti Ka Rishta**: The reciprocal rights have fostered deep socio-cultural bonds, often referred to as 'Roti-Beti' (marriage and familial ties), particularly among the communities living in the **Terai** region of Nepal and the Indian states of **Bihar** and **Uttar Pradesh**.
 
• **Sovereignty**: Contrary to misconceptions, the treaty does not place the **Nepalese Army** under Indian command; Nepal remains a fully sovereign nation with its own independent military and **Constitution**, which was most recently promulgated in **2015**.
